title: Lesson 28 - Governance implementation scenarios: data dictionary, ownership, quality metrics, tools
description: Compare and contrast various approaches and considerations for designing and implementing an enterprise data governance program, applying them in scenarios through the data dictionary, data ownership, quality metrics, and supporting tooling.

questions.question: A governance program measures a 22% duplicate rate on Accounts but duplicates persist. What is the missing component?
options: An issue-management workflow with owners and SLAs to resolve the duplicates
questions.explanation: Metrics identify the problem; resolution needs a workflow with accountability and SLAs. More metrics (A) or a bigger dictionary (C) do not fix data, and encryption (D) is unrelated.

questions.question: Which TWO dimensions describe data quality that a governance scorecard should track?
questions.explanation: Completeness/uniqueness (A) and consistency/timeliness (C) are core data-quality dimensions; infrastructure and layout counts are not data-quality measures.

questions.question: What distinguishes an accountable data owner from a technical custodian in a governance model?
options: The owner runs the systems; the custodian defines meaning
The owner is accountable for the domain's meaning/use; the custodian operates the systems
questions.explanation: The business owner is accountable for meaning and use while the custodian operates the technology; the other options invert or dismiss the roles.
